# Nobel Peace Prize — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/nobel-peace-prize.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/nobel-peace-prize.ttl`](../decks/nobel-peace-prize.ttl) · **Cards:** 106 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

Every Nobel Peace Prize from 1901 to 2025, one card per prize year: 106 cards with the year on the front and the laureate or laureates (people and organisations) on the back, with a short note where it helps, for example where the prize was awarded a year late, posthumously or declined, where a laureate received more than one Nobel Prize, or where an organisation has changed its name. Years with no award are left out; the deck ends with the 2025 prize, as the 2026 prize had not been announced when the deck was made on 4 October 2026. From the Nobel Prize API and Wikidata, checked against NobelPrize.org. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation or the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two sources whose terms allow that: the Nobel Prize API, whose terms say the service is "free to use according to the Creative Commons Zero (CC0) license", and Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0. The selection (every prize year with an award), the laureates and their order, the English names and most Swedish names, and the facts in the notes come from the API, cross-checked with Wikidata; the established Swedish forms and the few English corrections come from Wikidata's labels and aliases, except four Swedish orthographic or usage corrections confirmed by verification sources (FN:s barnfond and Den 14:e Dalai lama by the Swedish Wikipedia, Internationella rödakorskommittén by the Swedish Red Cross statutes, Rödakorsföreningarnas förbund by Swedish government bills and Riksdag records); the notes are in the authoring agent's own words. Four sources were used for verification only and contributed nothing but confirmation of single facts and spellings: NobelPrize.org's pages (copyright Nobel Prize Outreach: "You may not reproduce, distribute ... or otherwise use the Content without prior written permission"), read to confirm what the open sources give — the evidence quotes each year's one-sentence award statement from that year's summary page (a short quotation, to show what was checked; the same facts are CC0 from the same maker through the API, and the quotes are in the provenance report, not on the cards), but no text, selection or data field was taken, which also keeps clear of the EU sui generis database right (Directive 96/9/EC) in the site as a whole; the Swedish Wikipedia's list of laureates (CC BY-SA 4.0), compared with the Swedish names but not copied, its selection not used (copying the list would have made the deck CC BY-SA); the Swedish Red Cross statutes (no licence stated), which confirm the spelling of one Swedish name; and Swedish government bills and Riksdag records (not protected by copyright under 9 § of the Swedish Copyright Act), which confirm another. A spelling is a fact, not a protected expression. The API terms say that, in case of conflict, they prevail over CC0, and they add conditions for applications: not to alter the data or mislead users — the deck changes the API's English names in five documented places only (a trailing space removed, two accents restored, a country added, an organisation's own name instead of its English translation) and its Swedish names only where Swedish has an established form, each documented — and to credit the API as the data source, which the deck does. They also say applications may not use Nobel Prize Outreach's name or trademarks "in their titles or logos, or in any way that implies endorsement", and NobelPrize.org's terms of use (https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use/) list "Nobel Prize®" among the Nobel Foundation's registered trademarks and say "you may not use the Nobel Foundation trademarks without prior written permission from the Nobel Foundation". The deck's title, "Nobel Peace Prize" / "Nobels fredspris", uses the prize's name only to say what the deck is about (descriptive use: there is no other way to name the subject), with no logo, medal or other Nobel graphics, and its description says it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation or the Norwegian Nobel Committee. As for the literature deck, whether that satisfies the API terms' "titles" clause is a judgement for the publisher, flagged for Anton Wiklund before release; the fallback is a title without the prize's name, such as "Peace laureates 1901–2025" / "Fredspristagare 1901–2025".

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction. The deck was then cross-checked by independent AI reviewers (quality-control rounds 1–4: factual accuracy; language, translation and language tags; licensing, attribution and documentation; a re-check of the changed cards and a sample), whose findings were verified against the sources and applied or rejected with reasons, and by machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Prizes and selection. On 2026-10-04 the Nobel Prize API was queried for all Nobel Peace Prizes (nobelPrizeCategory=pea, sorted by year; see Queries) and for all peace laureates. It returned 125 prize years, 1901–2025, and 140 laureates. Nineteen years have no laureates: 1914, 1915, 1916, 1918, 1923, 1924, 1928, 1932, 1939, 1940, 1941, 1942, 1943, 1948, 1955, 1956, 1966, 1967 and 1972; NobelPrize.org's summary page for each of them says "No Nobel Prize was awarded this year". They are left out. Each of the other 106 years became one card, with the year (the API's awardYear, the year the prize is for) on the front, tagged zxx as a number in no language.
3. Back: English. The laureates of each year, in the order the API lists them, joined with ", " and " and " (three laureates in 1994, 2011 and 2022). The English names are the API's knownName.en (people) or orgName.en (organisations), the names under which the Nobel Foundation lists the laureates, unchanged except in five places: the API's "Le Duc Tho " has a trailing space, removed; "Maria Corina Machado" is written "María Corina Machado", her Spanish name and Wikidata's English and language-independent label (as the literature deck restored the accent in Miguel Ángel Asturias); "Oscar Arias Sánchez" is likewise written "Óscar Arias Sánchez", Wikidata's English label (added in quality-control round 2); "National Dialogue Quartet" is written "Tunisian National Dialogue Quartet", Wikidata's English label, since the bare name does not say which country (NobelPrize.org's summary has the country only in the motivation: "a pluralistic democracy in Tunisia"); and "Doctors Without Borders" is written "Médecins Sans Frontières", Wikidata's English label and the title of the laureate's facts page on NobelPrize.org (the summary page gives both: "Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders)"). Titles in the Nobel Foundation's names are kept (Sir Austen Chamberlain, Sir Norman Angell, Lord Boyd Orr, Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood).
4. Back: Swedish. The same laureates joined with ", " and " och ". Each Swedish name is the API's Swedish name (knownName.se / orgName.se) unless Swedish has an established form that differs, taken from Wikidata's Swedish label (query 2): Henri Dunant (API "Henry Dunant"), Robert Cecil, 1:e viscount Cecil av Chelwood (API "Robert Cecil, Vicomte Cecil av Chelwood"), Eisaku Sato, Anwar Sadat, Yassir Arafat, FN:s klimatpanel (API "Förenta Nationernas klimatpanel"; Wikidata's sv alias, chosen in round 2 over the sv label "Förenta nationernas klimatpanel" to match the deck's other FN:s names and the Swedish Wikipedia list), FN:s fredsbevarande styrkor (API "Förenta Nationernas fredsbevarande styrkor"), Tunisiens nationella dialogkvartett (API "Kvartetten för nationell dialog"), Världslivsmedelsprogrammet (API "World Food Programme"), Dmitrij Muratov, Ales Bjaljatski, María Corina Machado and Institut de droit international (API "Institutet för internationell rätt", a translation not found in use; Wikidata's Swedish label and the Swedish Wikipedia list both use the French name). Swedish orthography writes only the first word of an organisation's name with a capital, so the API's "Förenta Nationerna" and "Europeiska Unionen" are "Förenta nationerna" and "Europeiska unionen" (Wikidata's Swedish labels), "FNs barnfond" is "FN:s barnfond" (the genitive colon after an abbreviation; the form in the Swedish Wikipedia list; Wikidata's Swedish label is only "Unicef"), and "Internationella Rödakorskommittén" (API and Wikidata) is "Internationella rödakorskommittén", as the Swedish Red Cross writes it in its statutes (verification), and "Den 14:e Dalai Lama" is "Den 14:e Dalai lama" (Swedish capitalises only Dalai in the title, as in the Swedish Wikipedia's articles Dalai lama and Tenzin Gyatso; round 2). "Óscar Arias Sánchez" has its accent in Swedish too (the Swedish Wikipedia's article gives it as his full name; round 2). Two organisations have no established Swedish name and keep their own name in Swedish, as both the API and Wikidata do: the 1947 Friends Service Council and American Friends Service Committee (the API's "Vännernas samfunds råd" and "Vännernas samfund i USA" are not in use, and the second means the Quakers in the USA, not the committee). The 1963 League of Red Cross Societies is "Rödakorsföreningarnas förbund", its name in Swedish government bills and Riksdag records of 1947–1990 (found with the Riksdag open-data search, see Queries; round 2); the API gives only the federation's present Swedish name, which the note gives. Every Swedish name was then compared with the chronological list of laureates on the Swedish Wikipedia (verification only).
5. Second source for every laureate. Wikidata was queried (query 1) for every item with P166 award received = Q35637 (Nobel Peace Prize) and the year of its P585 point in time qualifier. All 140 laureates in the API were matched by the Wikidata id the API itself gives (laureate.wikidata.id) and all have Q35637 with the API's year, except one: Wikidata dates the United Nations' (Q1065) prize 2002, not 2001 (see Quality control). Wikidata also gives the prize to four items that are not laureates in the API: the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement (Q7178; 1917, 1944, 1963), the Quakers (Q170208; 1947, with the two laureate organisations as P1875 represented by), Human Rights Watch (Q187052; 1997, with qualifier P1416 affiliation = International Campaign to Ban Landmines) and the United Nations again (2002). They are not added: the Nobel Foundation's laureates are the ICRC, the two Quaker organisations and the ICBL (query 3).
6. Third source. NobelPrize.org's summary page for each year 1901–2025 and the facts page of each of the 140 laureates were fetched (one request per second, scripts fetch_summary.py and fetch_facts.py) and compared with the cards: the laureates and the order of their names, the 19 years without an award, the twelve prizes received a year later, Hammarskjöld's posthumous prize and Le Duc Tho's declined prize all agree with the API. NobelPrize.org is copyrighted and used for verification only.
7. Notes. The backNote is given only where it adds something the year and the names do not say, and each note's fact comes from the API or Wikidata: prizes awarded a year late (1912, 1919, 1925, 1929, 1933, 1935, 1944, 1952, 1954, 1960, 1962, 1976: the API's dateAwarded falls in the next year, and every summary page says the laureate "received his Nobel Prize one year later"); Dag Hammarskjöld's posthumous prize (1961; API death date 1961-09-18, award 1961-10-23; Wikidata P570); Le Duc Tho's declined prize (1973; API prizeStatus "declined"); the ICRC's three prizes and UNHCR's two (API laureate records); Linus Pauling's earlier Nobel Prize in Chemistry (API laureate record; Wikidata P166 Q44585); the present names of the Permanent International Peace Bureau and the League of Red Cross Societies (Wikidata's English labels of the same items); and that the 1947 laureates were two Quaker relief organisations, one British and one American (the countries in the API's founded.place and Wikidata's P17 country; Wikidata's Quakers statement P1875 represented by names both). The note first gave the founding places, London and Washington, D.C., from the API's founded.place and the facts pages; review round 1 found the AFSC was founded in Philadelphia (Wikidata P159; the AFSC's own history page), so the places were removed. The Swedish notes are the authoring agent's own translation; "tilldelas" (the award decision, as in the API's dateAwarded) takes its recipient (honom, dem, kommittén, flyktingkommissariatet). The laureates' countries were not used: many laureates had several, and for organisations the notion does not apply.
8. Machine checks. Every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build nobel-peace-prize) against live Wikidata: for every laureate, P166 includes Q35637; the English and the Swedish name on the card is a Wikidata label or alias in that language (or the language-independent "mul" label) where Wikidata has that form; and the facts behind the notes (the renamed organisations' labels and aliases, Q1267 P570 1961, Q48983 P166 Q44585, Q677499 P17 Q145 and Q464677 P17 Q30). The checks read only truthy property values and cannot see the P585 year qualifier, so the link between year and laureate — the core fact of each card — is verified by query 1, not on every build. Name checks are left out where the card's form is not on Wikidata in that language; every such name was confirmed against the API and NobelPrize.org (English) or the API, the Swedish Wikipedia list and, for the ICRC, the Swedish Red Cross (Swedish); they are listed in Quality control. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (node scripts/validate_sources.ts nobel-peace-prize).
9. Study direction. Front to back only: the ICRC (1917, 1944, 1963) and UNHCR (1954, 1981) won more than once, so a back does not always lead to one year.
10. Reproduction. The cards were generated from the saved API and Wikidata responses by a script (gen_cards.py) that applies the name decisions in steps 3 and 4 (Back: English and Back: Swedish) (and no other transformation: every other name is the API's), joins the names, writes the evidence of each card from the saved responses and NobelPrize.org pages, and adds the Wikidata checks; the review rounds' changes were then made by hand in the dossier. The scripts (gen_cards.py, fetch_summary.py, fetch_facts.py, runq.sh) and all raw responses are kept in the authoring agent's scratch directory, not in the repository, so the generation step itself cannot be rerun from the repository; the queries and URLs below are enough to fetch the same data again and the rules above to rebuild the cards.

## Selection

All 106 years from 1901 to 2025 in which the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded, one card per year, with every laureate of that year, people and organisations alike: the complete set, nothing chosen. Left out: the 19 years with no award (1914, 1915, 1916, 1918, 1923, 1924, 1928, 1932, 1939, 1940, 1941, 1942, 1943, 1948, 1955, 1956, 1966, 1967, 1972), since a card for them would have no laureate to learn; and the 2026 prize, which is announced on 9 October 2026 and had not been when this deck was made on 4 October 2026. Le Duc Tho's declined prize (1973) is included, as the Nobel Foundation lists him as a laureate; the note says so. The year is the prize year, not the year it was awarded or handed over: the 1912 prize, awarded in 1913, is on the card 1912. Organisations that are not laureates but that Wikidata also credits with a prize (the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, the Quakers, Human Rights Watch) are not on the cards.

## Queries

**All Nobel Peace Prizes, by year (saved as prizes.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Peace Prizes and peace laureates (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o prizes.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/nobelPrizes?nobelPrizeCategory=pea&limit=200&sort=asc&format=json"
```

**All peace laureates, with names, prize status, death dates, Wikidata ids and links to their facts pages (saved as laureates.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Peace Prizes and peace laureates (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o laureates.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureates?nobelPrizeCategory=pea&limit=200&format=json"
```

**The API terms of use (CC0)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Peace Prizes and peace laureates (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o terms.html "https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use-for-api-nobelprize-org-and-data-nobelprize-org/"
```

**How every SPARQL query below was run (runq.sh <name>, e.g. "runq.sh q1"): the query saved as a file (q1.rq, q2.rq, q3.rq) in the scratch directory D and sent to the Wikidata Query Service; expanded for q1:** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -G https://query.wikidata.org/sparql --data-urlencode query@/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo--claude-worktrees-authored-decks/0d3ab5ce-8aa3-4420-b0eb-935ec077f401/scratchpad/decks/nobel-peace-prize/q1.rq -H "Accept: application/sparql-results+json" -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o /tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo--claude-worktrees-authored-decks/0d3ab5ce-8aa3-4420-b0eb-935ec077f401/scratchpad/decks/nobel-peace-prize/q1.json
```

**Query 1 (q1.rq): every holder of the Nobel Peace Prize with the year and English, Swedish and language-independent labels and the Swedish Wikipedia article** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?enLabel ?svLabel ?mulLabel ?year ?svwiki WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q35637 ; pq:P585 ?date .
  BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year)
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?enLabel . FILTER(LANG(?enLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?svLabel . FILTER(LANG(?svLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?mulLabel . FILTER(LANG(?mulLabel) = "mul") }
  OPTIONAL { ?svwiki schema:about ?laureate ; schema:isPartOf <https://sv.wikipedia.org/> . }
}
ORDER BY ?year ?enLabel
```

**Query 2 (q2.rq): the English, Swedish and "mul" labels and aliases of every holder of the prize, to see which names on the cards Wikidata has** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?kind ?text WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q35637 .
  { ?laureate rdfs:label ?text . BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?laureate skos:altLabel ?text . BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
```

**Query 3 (q3.rq): the Nobel Peace Prize statements, with ranks and qualifiers, of the four items that query 1 found but the API does not list as laureates for that year** (Wikidata)


## Quality control

6 rounds, 37 findings: 30 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 7 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (410 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Completeness and correctness against the sources; agreement between the Nobel Prize API, Wikidata, NobelPrize.org and the Swedish Wikipedia; Wikidata machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 106 cards

The API's 125 prize years (106 with an award, 19 without) and 140 laureates were matched one by one against Wikidata's P166 Q35637 statements with their P585 years and against NobelPrize.org's summary page for every year and facts page for every laureate. The laureates and years agree in all three, except one wrong year on Wikidata (the United Nations, 2001). The 19 years without an award, the twelve late prizes, the posthumous and the declined prize agree between the API and NobelPrize.org. All 410 Wikidata checks of the time passed in the build (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py check nobel-peace-prize, 2026-10-04); later rounds added, changed and removed checks, see rounds 1–4. At the time of round 0 no independent review round had been run. Discrepancies and how they were resolved: The P166 checks confirm that each laureate received the prize but cannot see the year; the year of each card rests on the API, NobelPrize.org and query 1 (the P585 years), as method step 8 (Machine checks) says.

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 106 cards against a fresh pull of the Nobel Prize API (nobelPrizes and laureates, peace) and a Wikidata SPARQL query of P166 Q35637 with P585 years; the 19 years without an award, the twelve late prizes, the posthumous, declined and repeated prizes, the 2025 laureate and the 2026 cut-off; the notes.

Every year, laureate and note agreed with the sources except one: the 1947 note's founding places, where the American Friends Service Committee was founded in Philadelphia, not Washington, D.C. Fixed. Of two suggestions on the Wikidata checks, one was applied (a check on a non-laureate item dropped) and one was documented in the round-0 summary.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1947-friends-service-council-afsc | The note said the two laureates were "founded in London and in Washington, D.C."; the AFSC was founded in Philadelphia. The only support was NobelPrize.org's facts pages, a verification-only source that also gives the Friends Service Council's founding as 1647, and Wikidata has no P740 for the AFSC. | Verified: Wikidata Q464677 has P159 headquarters and P131 Philadelphia, P571 1917-04-30, P17 United States and no P740; the AFSC's own history page (https://afsc.org/history, fetched 2026-10-04, CC BY-NC-ND 2.0, consulted only) says "In 1917, a group of Quakers in Philadelphia founded AFSC". The API's laureate records give the same wrong values as the facts pages (509: founded 1917, Washington, D.C.; 508: founded 1647, London, the Religious Society of Friends' date; Wikidata dates the Council 1927). The note is now en "Two Quaker relief organisations, one British and one American." / sv "Två kväkarorganisationer för hjälparbete, en brittisk och en amerikansk.", from the countries in the API's founded.place and Wikidata P17 (checks Q677499 P17 Q145 and Q464677 P17 Q30 added). The facts-page evidence is kept as verification with the error noted; method step 7 (Notes), the nobelprize-org and nobel-prize-api usedFor and the round-0 finding were corrected. | fixed |
| 1947-friends-service-council-afsc | The check Q170208 (Quakers) P166 Q35637 checks an item that is not on the card and not a laureate. | Agreed: dropped. Wikidata's Quakers statement stays documented in the evidence and in round 0. | fixed |
| deck | The P166 = Q35637 checks cannot see the P585 year, so they confirm the award but not the year on the card (the ICRC, UNHCR and the UN's wrong 2002 on Wikidata). | Method step 8 (Machine checks) already says so and that the years were verified by query 1; a sentence saying that the P166 checks confirm the award but not the year, and that each year rests on the API, NobelPrize.org and query 1, was added to the round-0 summary.
